How an idea becomes a website that works

Not just the result, but the thinking behind it: what had to come across, who the site was for and why it’s structured the way it is.

Save Point

A desk with a socket and coffee ready on the minute

Field
Café & coworking
Task
Move choosing a seat and ordering online, and lead visitors to book a desk or pre-order a drink.
Solution
The site speaks its audience’s language: the interface is styled as a 90s gaming terminal, with TABLE_BOOKING.SYS and INVENTORY_MENU.DAT windows and a “checkpoint loaded” tag. The name Save Point becomes a promise: here you can “save your game” — grab a desk in advance instead of wasting time looking for a seat.
My role
Niche research, copy, design, build and launch
Live site

ELARA Dental

Dentistry where you know the price before treatment

Field
Dental clinic
Task
Give a new clinic with no reviews real reasons to be trusted, and lead visitors to book a consultation with a treatment plan.
Solution
A new clinic has no reviews, and the site doesn’t pretend otherwise. Instead of social proof it offers verifiable facts: CBCT and panoramic X-rays on site, a treatment plan with the total in your hands, and an honest “be the first to leave a review” badge.
My role
Niche research, copy, design, build and launch
Live site

Alba

Beauty in 90 minutes · time for yourself

Field
Beauty salon
Task
Ease a client’s three biggest fears — “they’ll ruin my hair”, “it’ll take half my day”, “the price will change” — and lead her to book via a form or WhatsApp.
Solution
The headline “Beauty in 90 minutes” turns a vague “quick” into a concrete fact, while the “time for yourself” concept and the premium visit scenario make saving time part of the Alba brand’s value.

Tropinka

School readiness and development for ages 3–6

Field
Kids’ center
Task
Calm the parental worry of “are we already too late?”, explain the teaching approach and programs clearly, and move hesitant parents to book a trial class.
Solution
The “Thought → Movement → Creativity” design block visualises the center’s method instead of just describing it. Parents grasp Tropinka’s approach before reading the program, while the soft natural palette and the image of a path create a sense of safety and care from the very first second.

Aigerim & Timur

A wedding where every guest knows their table and their ride

Field
Wedding invitation
Task
Gather everything at one address and get an answer from every guest about attendance, the hot dish and transfer.
Solution
The site speaks in the couple’s voice: “Three years, two peaks and one cable-car queue”, a joke about three coffee machines in the wishlist and a Kazakh greeting, “Тойымызға қош келдіңіздер!”, on the first screen. Practical blocks — seating, transfer, the form — come through the couple’s character, so the information never reads like instructions.

Mission “Miron-7”

A birthday as a space flight with a boarding pass

Field
Kids’ birthday party
Task
Turn an organisational mailing into a game that adults and kids both enjoy.
Solution
All the party logistics are presented as a space flight: the invitation is an “invitation on board”, registration is a “boarding pass” and wishes go into a “ship’s log”. The interface stays clear for parents, while the child gets a rocket and a boarding pass of their own; thick outlines and orange-pink accents on pale blue keep the mood of a cartoon game.

A website that answers doubts — so you don’t have to

The client is already interested. But they still need to make up their mind.

They found you on 2GIS. Checked your Instagram. Maybe even opened your website. But questions remain:

  • Is this service right for me?
  • Can I trust you?
  • How does it all work?
  • How much will it cost?
  • What happens after I get in touch?

Without answers, people fill in the gaps themselves. Sometimes they just put the decision off — or go with whoever was easier to understand.

How I work

What actually happens, from brief to finished site.

  1. Brief

    You fill in a short brief — about 15 minutes of your time. You tell me about your business, your clients and what’s currently getting in the way of enquiries.

    Outcome: a clear task and a starting point for research.

    Fill in the brief

  2. Research

    I study your niche, your clients and how they go about choosing a service like yours. I look at competitors’ sites and real reviews to see which questions, expectations and objections need answering.

    Outcome: a clear picture of your audience, what they want and what your offer can be built on.

  3. Offer & structure

    I work out what to show first, which questions to answer and how to lead visitors to get in touch. I put together a page prototype and agree it with you before development starts.

    Outcome: the page logic, section structure and a clear offer.

  4. Copy, design & build

    I turn your strengths into clear messages, a visual system and an easy-to-use interface. Then I show you a working draft — all changes at this stage are free.

    Outcome: approved copy, design and a working draft of the site.

  5. Launch

    I test the site on different devices, connect your domain and set up enquiries to arrive in Telegram. You get an archive of all the files and a short video guide.

    Outcome: a live website, ready to receive enquiries.

Honest answers — before you even ask

What if I don’t like what you come up with?

We go step by step, so there are no surprises. First we agree on the structure and copy (the prototype), and only then do I move on to visuals and the build. All changes at the draft stage are included in the price. We keep refining until you like the site and it works for your clients.

What if I don’t have copy, a logo or decent photos?

That’s common. I take care of all the copy: I interview you, study your clients’ reviews and write clear, meaningful headlines. For visuals, I’ll help you find quality graphics, put together a neat logo and build a consistent style.

Is the $265 base package really enough, or will I end up paying extra?

The package covers everything: from research and copy to the build, mobile optimisation and setting up enquiries to arrive in Telegram. You only pay extra for add-ons you choose yourself (second language, calculator or quiz, express delivery — prices are in the “Add-ons” section) and for direct service costs: a domain (usually around $7–10 a year) and hosting, if you need a paid plan.

How long does it take, and how involved do I need to be?

Development takes 5 to 12 working days. From you, it takes about 15–20 minutes to fill in the brief at the start, plus quick approvals at two stages (structure and final draft). No endless calls — everything clear and to the point.

What happens after launch? What if something breaks?

After handover you get 30 days of free technical support. If you spot a mistake or want to tweak some text, I’ll fix it free of charge. You also get an archive of the files and a short video guide, so the project stays fully under your control.

How does payment work, and is there a contract?

Yes, everything is official. We set out the stages and commitments in a written agreement. Payment is split into two equal parts: 50% before work starts and 50% only after you approve the finished working draft, before it goes live.

Why do I need a website if I already have Instagram?

Instagram works well with people who already follow you. A website answers questions before anyone has to message you: what you offer, what it costs, how it works and why you can be trusted. People find it through search and via the link on 2GIS, and enquiries land straight in your Telegram. Instagram and a website don’t compete — the site link fits perfectly in your bio.

Do you guarantee I’ll get enquiries?

The number of enquiries depends on traffic, demand and the service itself, so I won’t promise specific numbers — that wouldn’t be honest. What I’m responsible for is that anyone who lands on your site quickly understands your offer, finds answers to their doubts and can get in touch in a couple of taps.

Who owns the website after launch?

You do. After launch I hand over an archive of all the files and a short video guide. The site isn’t tied to me — any developer can move it or build on it.
